Distance is a huge lot of fun.

Don't think of it as a racing game, but rather as a platformer with a car: the entire point is getting to the end of the levels, going over jumps, avoiding lasers that can cut off your wheels and make the car uncontrollable, anticipating pop-up obstacles, flying through hoops, dodging spikes, etc. Though a lot of effort has been made when it comes to official levels, the selection is still mediocre and the real meat of the game is the Workshop: tons and tons of fanmade levels, of all styles.

The environments are overly colourful with neons and flashing lights everywhere, often in synch with the Eurobass music (which just looks and feels perfect in motion). The official levels severely underuse their assets: again, if you want varied scenery, a wide range of difficulty levels, and more, it's Workshop or bust.

The controls are very precise though you are often going fast enough that a minor and understandable mistake will bring you back to the last checkpoint, which thankfully is rarely far away. The use of physics is interesting: oftentimes, you are driving sideways or upside-down, and slowing down too much would cause you to fall off the track. Sometimes, even driving normally will cause you to fly off (too fast in a strong downwards curve) unless you use the thrusters to cling to the track or land sooner after a jump.

It can sound overwhelming and out of reach to someone who isn't a platform enthusiasm, but it is absolutely not the case, the game is very approachable and all of this feels reasonable and natural.

If you are interested but unsure, you can simply download the "demo" (it's a full game but intended as a proof of concept), Nitronic Rush:

http://nitronic-rush.com/download-game/

A lot have changed since, but playing Nitronic Rush will give you a good idea of what Distance is about.
